newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian police seize arms at remote militia camp.
newsitem.headline: Canadian police seize arms at remote militia camp.

text.p: Canadian police said on Friday they had seized weapons and survival gear from what they believe is a training camp for a right-wing U.S. militia in the remote mountains of northern British Columbia.

No arrests were made and police did not identify the group involved. More details were to be announced later in the day at a news conference in this small town about 425 miles (640 km) north of Vancouver, near the Alaska border.
The weapons seized included automatic rifles and a 0.50-calibre machine gun, which are all prohibited in Canada.
The raid occurred three months ago but police did not release any information until now while they investigated the people who set up the camp.
Royal Canadian Mounted Police spokesman Peter Montague said suspects in the case were in the United States and U.S. law enforcement authorities were also working on the case.
"It's quite frightening," he said. "We've never seen anything like this here."
The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation in July arrested eight members of a Washington state militia in Bellingham, just over the British Columbia border. They were charged with conspiracy.
Police are investigating possible links between U.S. militias and right-wing groups in British Columbia, according to Vancouver newspapers.
